env.name: cmv
env.description:
Measure the supplied hypotheses; do not discover, rewrite or refine them. Each feature is
one scalar measurement of a discussion row, not a separate observation for every comment.
The full supplied corpus contains 2,000 rows: 1,000 changed and 1,000 unchanged outcomes.
Describe associations, not proven causal effects or prospective prediction.

Columns:
  - post_created_utc: Unix timestamp for the original post, not a comment or score-measurement
    timestamp. Response delay cannot be calculated from it.
  - title: the original poster's (OP's) heading or claim statement, not the argument body.
  - argument: the OP's explanation of their view. Use this field for argument-body measurements;
    include title only when the requested scope includes the heading or when it is needed to
    interpret a comment's target. Text can contain quotations, edits and outcome announcements.
  - OC_comments: a JSON-encoded list of available counter-argument comments by OTHER users,
    not the OP. Parse the list before counting comments, words or semantic instances.
    Specify any/all/count/share/mean explicitly. List order is not rank, importance or chronology.
    If properties must coexist in one comment, assess their conjunction within that comment;
    separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. The row-level extractor still returns one scalar.
    List length counts comments, not necessarily distinct commenters. No per-comment outcomes,
    scores or timestamps are supplied. OP-language measurements use title/argument instead.
  - conversation: formatted interaction text overlapping OC_comments, not extra independent
    evidence. It may include later replies and explicit view-change announcements. Do not use
    it as an initial-argument snapshot. When interaction is required, specify speaker/turn
    selection and use it only if faithful measurement is possible under the leakage guard below.
  - log_length: a supplied log-transformed length measure. Construction, source text, log base
    and timing are undocumented. When named by the hypothesis, use the supplied value and state
    that limitation; do not equate it with argument word count or reconstruct its log base.
  - post_score: the observed original-post score, not a comment score, voter count or initial
    endorsement. Its measurement time relative to the outcome is unknown; post_created_utc
    does not establish that timing.
  - delta: OUTCOME, 1 if the OP changed their view, else 0. Never a predictor or annotation input.
  - post_id, comment_id: identifiers, never predictors.

Attribution and unavailable measurements:
  - No measured personality scores, Big Five questionnaires or author demographics are supplied.
    A personality inference from writing is a linguistic proxy, not an observed trait; do not
    substitute it silently when the hypothesis requires an unavailable measurement.
  - Distinguish the author's own assertions or experiences from attributed quotations.
    An external source cited as support can count for an evidence feature without making the
    source's wording or experience the author's own. Background/rebuttal quotations are not
    automatically adopted support. Apply this distinction to OP text and other users' comments.
    Quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker.

Predictor leakage guard (applies to every text field):
  - Never use the OP's own view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or
    resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred as predictor evidence.
    This exclusion applies even inside argument and even if such text expresses the construct.
    Generic discussion of platform/delta rules is not an outcome announcement; retain relevant
    discussion rather than blanket-removing mentions of delta.
  - Subject to this guard, measure supplied current text unless the hypothesis restricts time.
    Deleting marked edits or outcome announcements does not reconstruct initial/pre-outcome
    text. Neither post_created_utc nor unordered comments supplies missing comment/edit times.
    An edit marker alone does not establish when an edit occurred.
    If faithful exposure requires unavailable temporal information, state that limitation and
    set term=null; do not substitute current text or infer a snapshot.
  - delta remains the fixed outcome. A hypothesis requiring another outcome or outcome-reporting
    text as a predictor is unsupported: explain the limitation and set term=null.
    If excluding outcome evidence changes the requested predictor itself, preserve the original
    claim as unsupported; do not silently replace it with a cleaned concession/attitude proxy.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument includes explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms are associated with lower view change than those without such comparisons.

features.name: argument_compares_to_established_norms
features.definition: OP argument: explicitly compares the OP's view or case to an established scientific or historical norm, standard, consensus or precedent.
features.spec: Read only the OP's argument text (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the argument explicitly compares the OP's position, claim or case to an established scientific norm/standard/consensus or an established historical norm/standard/precedent (the comparison must be stated, not merely implied by topic). Return 0 if the argument has no such explicit comparison. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible text but is not itself a scientific/historical comparison. Do not treat quotations of others as the OP's own comparison unless the OP adopts them. Return null if the argument is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: There is no association between argument_compares_to_established_norms and view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Rows with argument_compares_to_established_norms=1 have lower delta than rows with 0.
decomposed.note: Measured on current supplied argument text (including marked edits) after excluding outcome announcements; initial snapshot is not reconstructed. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Arguments expressing explicit fear of social rejection or isolation are associated with lower view-change rates than arguments stating beliefs without emotional self-defense.

features.name: op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation
features.definition: OP title/argument: 1 if the OP explicitly expresses their own fear of social rejection or isolation (e.g., being ostracized, disliked, excluded) as part of stating or defending their view.
features.spec: Read the OP's title and argument (current text). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly expresses fear or worry of social rejection, ostracism, exclusion or isolation (for example, being disliked, shunned or left alone for holding or voicing the view). Return 0 if no such explicit fear is expressed (including when text only states beliefs, or expresses other emotions). Exclude quoted or reported words of others unless the OP adopts them as their own fear. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if inside argument or expressing the construct; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and is neither positive nor excluded evidence. Marked edits are current text and may be used unless they are outcome reporting. Do not infer an initial snapshot. If title and argument are both missing/empty or malformed, return null. Output a single 0/1 or null.

features.name: op_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense
features.definition: OP title/argument: 1 if the OP states their beliefs or reasons without any emotional self-defense (no defensive emotional self-protection or emotional appeal to shield themselves or the view).
features.spec: Read the OP's title and argument (current text). Return 1 if the OP states beliefs, claims or reasons in their own voice and the text contains no emotional self-defense, i.e. no defensive emotional self-protection, expressions of feeling threatened, hurt, fearful of rejection/isolation, or emotional appeals used to shield the OP or the view from challenge. Return 0 if the OP's text contains such emotional self-defense, or if it states no beliefs at all. Exclude quoted or reported others' words unless the OP adopts them. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if inside argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and is ignored as emotional evidence unless otherwise relevant. Marked edits are current text unless outcome reporting. Do not infer an initial snapshot. If title and argument are missing/empty or malformed, return null. Output a single 0/1 or null.

decomposed.h0: View-change rates do not differ between rows with op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation and rows with op_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense.
decomposed.h1: Rows with op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation have lower view-change rates than rows with op_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense.
decomposed.note: The claim compares group A (explicit fear) versus named group B (beliefs without emotional self-defense), not A versus not-A. In the joint OLS, each coefficient is relative to rows in neither group, so the A-versus-B contrast (beta_A - beta_B) is not a single design-matrix coefficient; term=null. Analysis would need subsetting to A or B rows or a linear contrast, not available here. Measures are current-text linguistic judgments of OP title/argument, not observed psychological states; no initial snapshot is reconstructed. Associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that cite specific, functioning institutional precedents are associated with a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract normative principles.

features.name: any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent
features.definition: Other-user comments: at least one comment cites a specific, actually functioning institutional precedent (an existing real institution, policy or system operating in practice) as support.
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse it; list order is not rank or chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment cites a specific, real, actually functioning institutional precedent (e.g., an existing law, policy, organization or system that operates in practice in some jurisdiction or institution) as support for its argument. Hypothetical, invented or merely proposed institutions, generic abstract principles, and vague unspecified references do not count. Verification externally is not required; use only the supplied text. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and is retained if relevant. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including an empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

features.name: any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles
features.definition: Other-user comments: at least one comment relies on abstract normative principles (moral, rights or fairness arguments).
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse it; list order is not rank or chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment relies on abstract normative principles, i.e., moral, rights, justice or fairness arguments about what ought to be, stated in general terms rather than via concrete cases. Purely factual, empirical or concrete-precedent arguments do not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and is retained if relevant. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including an empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: Rows with any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent have no higher delta probability than rows with any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles (equal association).
decomposed.h1: Comments citing functioning institutional precedents are associated with higher delta probability than comments relying on abstract normative principles.
decomposed.note: The claim is a contrast (precedent beta greater than normative beta), which no single coefficient in this OLS represents; beta_precedent alone is not beta_precedent minus beta_normative, so term=null. Features are row-level any-indicators and may overlap (a row can have both); comment-level comparison and exclusive groups are not available. OC_comments order is unknown; no per-comment outcomes. Associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring longer precomputed log-transformed discussion length are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: supplied_log_length
features.definition: Supplied precomputed log-transformed length measure of the discussion, used as given.
features.spec: Return pd.to_numeric(df['log_length'], errors='coerce') as a float; null if missing or non-numeric. Observed range about 0.69 to 7.44. Do not recompute, rescale, or infer the log base or source text.

decomposed.h0: supplied_log_length has no association with the likelihood of delta (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Higher supplied_log_length is associated with a higher likelihood of delta (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: log_length is a supplied value with undocumented construction, source text, log base and timing; it may include post-outcome text or later replies, and it is not equated with argument word count. Association only, not causal or prospective.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit admissions of uncertainty are associated with a higher probability of view change than those asserting absolute certainty.

features.name: op_argument_admits_uncertainty
features.definition: OP argument: 1 if the OP explicitly admits uncertainty or possible error in their own view (e.g., says they may be wrong or are unsure).
features.spec: Read only the OP's current argument text (column argument). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly expresses uncertainty about their view or admits they could be mistaken or lack certainty (e.g., 'I might be wrong', 'I'm not sure'). Return 0 if no such explicit admission appears. Exclude quotations of other people, opponents' positions, and moderator/bot notices unless the OP adopts them as their own. Exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred (including edits containing these); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not try to reconstruct an initial snapshot; use supplied current text only. If argument is missing or malformed, return null.

features.name: op_argument_asserts_absolute_certainty
features.definition: OP argument: 1 if the OP explicitly asserts absolute certainty about their own view (e.g., claims it is undeniably or certainly true, with no doubt).
features.spec: Read only the OP's current argument text (column argument). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly asserts absolute certainty about their view (e.g., 'there is no doubt', 'undeniably', 'I am 100% sure', 'objectively the case without exception'). Ordinary confident or opinionated statements without explicit absolute-certainty claims are 0. Return 0 if none appears. Exclude quotations of other people, opponents' positions, and moderator/bot notices unless the OP adopts them. Exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and text reporting whether the outcome occurred (including in edits); generic discussion of delta/platform rules remains eligible. Do not reconstruct an initial snapshot; use supplied current text only. If argument is missing or malformed, return null.

decomposed.h0: Rows whose op_argument_admits_uncertainty is 1 have the same probability of view change as rows with op_argument_asserts_absolute_certainty equal to 1.
decomposed.h1: Rows with op_argument_admits_uncertainty have a higher probability of view change than rows with op_argument_asserts_absolute_certainty.
decomposed.note: The claim compares uncertainty-admitting arguments with absolute-certainty-asserting arguments (named groups, not A vs not-A). No single OLS coefficient represents that contrast (beta_uncertainty - beta_certainty, and groups may overlap or both be 0), so term=null. Measures current argument text only, including edits, after excluding outcome-reporting text; initial pre-outcome argument cannot be reconstructed. Associations only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently challenging multiple distinct factual premises within the argument are positively associated with view change.

features.name: distinct_op_factual_premises_challenged
features.definition: Other-user comments: number of distinct factual premises stated in the OP's argument that are challenged by at least one comment (deduplicated across comments).
features.spec: Read OP title and argument (for context; premises must be factual claims made in the OP's argument text) and OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments; parse it). Count the distinct factual premises (empirical/factual claims, not values or purely normative claims) in the OP's argument that are challenged (disputed, contradicted, or shown to be false/unsupported with a factual objection) by at least one comment. Each distinct premise counts once even if several comments challenge it; one comment challenging two different premises counts both. Ignore challenges to the title's value judgments, to reasoning not tied to a stated factual premise, and to claims not made by the OP. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not such an announcement and remains eligible. Use supplied current text including marked edits; do not reconstruct an initial snapshot. Comment list order carries no meaning. Output a non-negative integer. Valid empty comment list -> 0. Missing/malformed OC_comments or missing argument -> null. No challenged factual premise -> 0.

features.name: challenges_multiple_distinct_op_factual_premises
features.definition: Other-user comments: 1 if the comments together challenge two or more distinct factual premises of the OP's argument.
features.spec: Using `distinct_op_factual_premises_challenged`: return null if df['distinct_op_factual_premises_challenged'] is null, else 1 if df['distinct_op_factual_premises_challenged'] >= 2, else 0.

decomposed.h0: challenges_multiple_distinct_op_factual_premises has no association with delta.
decomposed.h1: challenges_multiple_distinct_op_factual_premises is positively associated with delta.
decomposed.note: "Frequently" has no specified cutoff; "multiple" is operationalized as >=2 distinct premises challenged across the row's comments (any-row measure, not a frequency rate). Unordered comments, current argument text including edits (no initial snapshot). Association only, not causal. The count feature is retained as base measurement; the code feature is used for the test.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: oc_comment_count
features.definition: OC_comments: number of available counter-argument comments by other users in the parsed list.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list. Return len(list) as an integer (>=0). A valid empty list gives 0. Missing or malformed JSON gives null. Do not read any other column; counts comments, not distinct commenters.

decomposed.h0: oc_comment_count has no association with the likelihood of delta (OP view change).
decomposed.h1: Higher oc_comment_count is associated with a higher likelihood of delta, i.e. fewer counter-argument comments go with lower likelihood.
decomposed.note: Association only. OC_comments are only the available counter-argument comments, a possibly incomplete list; order and timing unknown. The hypothesis wording ("original argument contains fewer responses") is interpreted as the discussion's number of available counter-argument comments. No cutoff for "fewer" is specified, so a continuous count is used. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability approximation.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions with at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: distinct_counter_argument_count
features.definition: Other-user comments: number of distinct counter-arguments against the OP's view, deduplicated across comments (not the comment count).
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP), parsed as a list, with title and argument only as context to identify the OP's view. Return a non-negative integer: the number of semantically distinct counter-arguments to the OP's view made across all comments. Several comments making the same point count once; one comment making several different points counts each. Do not count agreement, questions, clarifications, jokes, or off-topic remarks. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if in argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement but is not itself a counter-argument unless it argues against the OP's view. Use current supplied text; list order is not rank or chronology. Valid empty list gives 0. Missing or malformed OC_comments gives null. Anchors: 0 = none, 1 = one distinct argument, 3 = three distinct arguments.

features.name: has_at_least_three_distinct_counter_arguments
features.definition: Other-user comments: 1 if there are at least three distinct counter-arguments to the OP's view.
features.spec: Using `distinct_counter_argument_count`: return null if df['distinct_counter_argument_count'] is null, else 1 if df['distinct_counter_argument_count'] >= 3, else 0.

decomposed.h0: has_at_least_three_distinct_counter_arguments has no association with the likelihood of delta.
decomposed.h1: Rows with has_at_least_three_distinct_counter_arguments = 1 have a higher likelihood of delta than rows with 0.
decomposed.note: Association only. Distinctness is a semantic judgment over available comments; OC_comments may be only a subset of the discussion, order/time unknown. Threshold of 3 is taken from the hypothesis. The code feature's source_columns list the original columns read by its upstream feature.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post title uses absolute certainty markers are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: title_uses_absolute_certainty_markers
features.definition: OP title: uses at least one absolute certainty marker (e.g., wording expressing total, unqualified certainty or universality such as always/never/all/obviously/undeniably).
features.spec: Read only the title (the OP's heading). Return 1 if the title contains at least one absolute certainty marker, i.e. wording that presents the claim with total, unqualified certainty or exceptionless universality (e.g. 'always', 'never', 'all', 'every', 'obviously', 'undeniably', 'definitely', 'no one'). The listed words are nonexhaustive examples; judge by meaning in context. Return 0 if the title is present and has no such marker (hedged or merely opinionated wording, e.g. 'generally', 'I think', does not count). Ignore the 'CMV:' prefix. Exclude any OP view-change/delta-award announcement, post-outcome thank-you/resolution update or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; if the title consists only of such text, treat it as having no marker. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement. Return null if the title is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: title_uses_absolute_certainty_markers is not associated with the likelihood of delta (OP changing view).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with title_uses_absolute_certainty_markers = 1 are associated with lower likelihood of delta than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Association only, not causal. Certainty markers are judged semantically from the current title; no intensity or frequency cutoff is specified by the hypothesis. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where original posts explicitly invite critique or use tentative language are associated with higher view-change rates than those using absolute, definitive declarations.

features.name: op_invites_critique_or_uses_tentative_language
features.definition: OP title/argument: 1 if the OP explicitly invites critique or challenge, or uses tentative/hedged language about their own view (e.g., expresses uncertainty or possible error).
features.spec: Read the OP's title and argument (current text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP's own text explicitly invites critique/counterargument/challenge to their view, OR expresses their own view with tentative, hedged or uncertain wording (e.g., possible error, openness to being wrong). Return 0 if neither is present. Ignore external quotations and moderator/bot notices unless the OP adopts them. Exclude entirely, as evidence, any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred (even within argument); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not try to reconstruct an initial version by removing edits. If both title and argument are missing or malformed, return null.

features.name: op_uses_absolute_definitive_declarations
features.definition: OP title/argument: 1 if the OP states their own view in absolute, definitive, certain declarations without hedging.
features.spec: Read the OP's title and argument (current text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP states their own view using absolute, definitive, certain declarations (e.g., claiming certainty, no possible exceptions or no room for doubt). Return 0 otherwise, including when the text is tentative, hedged or neutral. Ignore external quotations and moderator/bot notices unless the OP adopts them. Exclude entirely, as evidence, any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred (even within argument); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not try to reconstruct an initial version by removing edits. If both title and argument are missing or malformed, return null.

decomposed.h0: Rows with op_invites_critique_or_uses_tentative_language have the same view-change rate as rows with op_uses_absolute_definitive_declarations.
decomposed.h1: op_invites_critique_or_uses_tentative_language rows have higher view-change rates than op_uses_absolute_definitive_declarations rows.
decomposed.note: The claim is a contrast between tentative/inviting posts and absolute posts; this is not a single coefficient (it is beta_tentative minus beta_absolute, and the two features are not complements, so neither coefficient alone tests it), hence term=null. Measures current text including marked edits; initial pre-outcome OP text is unavailable. Associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that explicitly cite specific real-world examples are associated with higher likelihood of original view change.

features.name: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example
features.definition: Other-user comments: at least one comment explicitly cites a specific real-world example (actual case, event, entity or concrete personal experience; not hypothetical or invented).
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly cites a specific real-world example, i.e. an actual, particular case, event, person, organization, place, study or concrete personal experience offered as an example (a specific personal experience qualifies; no outside verification is needed). Hypothetical, invented or generic scenarios and vague generalities do not count. Do not use OP text. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies. A valid empty list gives 0. Missing or malformed input gives null. List order carries no meaning. Output a single 0/1 value.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example has no association with delta (view change).
decomposed.h1: Rows where any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example is 1 have higher likelihood of delta.
decomposed.note: Association only, not causal. "Featuring" is operationalized as at least one comment (any), with no frequency cutoff. OC_comments is an unordered list of available comments; no timing is available, and comments may have been posted after or before the OP's view change.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counterarguments containing measured, logical reasoning are positively associated with the original poster changing their mind compared to those containing emotional aggression in ChangeMyView discussions.

features.name: share_comments_measured_logical_reasoning
features.definition: Other-user counterargument comments: share of comments that present measured, logical reasoning (calm, evidence- or inference-based argument).
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse the list). For each comment, decide whether it contains measured, logical reasoning: a calm, coherent argument that supports its point with explicit inferences, evidence or reasoned steps, in a non-hostile tone. A comment may also contain aggression; judge this property independently. Return the number of comments with this property divided by the total number of comments (range 0-1). Empty valid list or missing/malformed input: return null. List order carries no meaning. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; do not use them as evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be retained. Use only current supplied text; do not infer timing.

features.name: share_comments_emotional_aggression
features.definition: Other-user counterargument comments: share of comments that contain emotional aggression (hostile, insulting, angry or belligerent tone toward the OP or view).
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse the list). For each comment, decide whether it contains emotional aggression: hostile, insulting, contemptuous, angry or belligerent language directed at the OP or their view. Mere disagreement, firm or blunt wording, or generic emotional language without hostility does not count. A comment may also contain logical reasoning; judge this property independently. Return the number of comments with emotional aggression divided by the total number of comments (range 0-1). Empty valid list or missing/malformed input: return null. List order carries no meaning. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; do not use them as evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be retained. Use only current supplied text; do not infer timing.

features.name: logical_minus_aggressive_comment_share
features.definition: Share of other-user counterargument comments with measured logical reasoning minus share with emotional aggression (range -1 to 1).
features.spec: Using `share_comments_measured_logical_reasoning` and `share_comments_emotional_aggression`: return df['share_comments_measured_logical_reasoning'] - df['share_comments_emotional_aggression']; null if either is null.

decomposed.h0: logical_minus_aggressive_comment_share has no association with delta (coefficient is zero).
decomposed.h1: Higher logical_minus_aggressive_comment_share (more measured logical reasoning relative to emotional aggression) is associated with greater likelihood of delta.
decomposed.note: Operationalizes the logical-vs-aggressive contrast as a difference of within-row comment shares, assuming equal weight for both shares; the hypothesis does not specify aggregation or frequency. The two properties are not mutually exclusive within a comment. Rows with empty comment lists are null. Comment order/timing unavailable; current text only. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote and refute specific factual claims in the original post are associated with higher rates of view change.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim
features.definition: Other-user comments: at least one single comment both explicitly quotes specific OP wording and refutes a factual claim in that quoted OP text.
features.spec: Read title, argument (OP text) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users, not the OP; parse it). Return 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly quotes or directly reproduces specific wording from the OP's title/argument (endorsement not required; quotation marks alone do not suffice unless the text matches the OP text) and (b) refutes, in that same comment, a factual claim contained in that quoted OP wording by arguing it is factually wrong. Quotation and refutation must be in the same comment and concern the same OP factual claim; separate comments cannot satisfy it. Refuting only opinions/values, or quoting without refuting, or refuting without quoting, gives 0. Use current supplied text including marked edits, but ignore as evidence any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred (even inside argument); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not such an announcement. Judge each comment separately; list order carries no meaning. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including a valid empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed, or if the OP title/argument is missing so that absence cannot be established (a clear positive match against available OP text still gives 1). Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if in the argument; do not use them as the quoted/referenced OP text or as evidence.
